elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2.2 reads "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ". The prior gates ($60 million of Development Costs funded; only "prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval") and the 300% Development Cost exit payment are gone, so the election is unconditional and available throughout the Term. There are no Order Forms in this co-development structure, and the element is disjunctive, so agreement-level coverage suffices. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" appears to be an alias-matching artifact (the customer here is "PB", not a listed alias); the substance is expressly present.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" — the redacted [***] notice period is replaced with a fixed 30-day written notice, at (not above) the preferred ceiling.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case SFJ will refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination" — express pro-rata refund obligation on the counterparty, tied to the convenience termination. Note (not a failure of the element, but a drafting repair worth making): this Agreement's payment flow runs from SFJ to PB for Development Costs, with PB paying Approval Payments only post-approval, so "prepaid fees" has no defined referent here; conforming it to "any amounts prepaid by PB to SFJ under this Agreement, if any" would avoid an inoperative mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: New 14.2.11: "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term." SFJ's retained exits are all event-triggered rather than convenience rights — 14.2.6 requires a Change of Control of PB and 14.2.10 requires PB's exercise of decision-making authority under 5.2.4 plus continued good-faith disagreement after Executive Officer escalation — so the bar is not internally contradicted. "Term" is a defined term (1.1.185 / Section 14.1), so the trigger is not undefined.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is "thirty (30) days' prior written notice", which sits at the preferred standard and outside the 60–90 day fallback band. This element is the sole reason the fallback checklist is incomplete; it is not a defect because the preferred level is fully met.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: "PB will owe SFJ no termination fee or other payment for such termination" — the 300% of Development Costs exit payment is deleted, and no retained formula, instalment, or contingent exit fee applies to a 14.2.2 termination (the retained Approval Payment obligation arises only if PB continues development and obtains Regulatory Approval, and is not a termination fee). A zero fee is within any three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: 14.2.11 removes SFJ's convenience right entirely during the Term, which is stronger than confining it to term end. SFJ's remaining 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 rights are event-triggered, not convenience rights.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with no SFJ convenience right under 14.2.11, there is no convenience notice period for SFJ to satisfy. No retained clause gives SFJ a short-notice no-cause exit.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (30-day PB convenience right, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on SFJ convenience termination during the Term). The deviation call is correct — the original 14.2.2 was gated on $60 million of SFJ funding, closed at first Regulatory Approval, carried a redacted notice period, and cost 300% of Development Costs, so it failed the fallback on material terms.

Minimality failure 1 — duplicative operative term: the added covenant "PB will owe SFJ no termination fee or other payment for such termination" restates the effect of deleting the 300% payment sentence. Repair: delete the 300% sentence and the trailing "reduced by the amount previously paid by PB to SFJ pursuant to this Section 14.2.2" credit, and drop the affirmative no-fee covenant.

Minimality failure 2 — benefit outside the checklist: recasting "in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results" as PB "will acquire the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4" converts a paid transfer into an uncompensated one. No T4C element requires a data-package entitlement. Repair: strike the exchange language altogether and let Section 11.1.1.4 govern the transfer and its consideration on its own terms, or retain a purchase construct decoupled from the deleted 300% figure.

Drafting repair (does not defeat any element): "prepaid fees" has no referent in this Agreement's payment architecture (SFJ funds Development Costs; PB pays Approval Payments only post-approval), so the refund sentence risks being inoperative. Conform to "any amounts prepaid by PB to SFJ under this Agreement, if any, for the period after the effective date of termination".

Intent preserved: SFJ's event-triggered exits (14.2.3 Material Adverse Event, 14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.10 JSC deadlock) and their payment formulas survive without contradiction with new 14.2.11; the Section 5.2.2.2 cross-reference to 14.2.10 and the ARTICLE 6 / Section 6.2 / Section 6.7 references in 14.2.2 remain intact, and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Fallback is not independently complete (30 days is outside the 60–90 day band), which is immaterial because the preferred checklist is satisfied; the margin comment correctly offers the 60–90 day / three-month-fee-cap fallback without relying on it for coverage.
